phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila takahashii (2.4 µm, detail scale)

predecessor.what_changes: The suzukii male apical wing spot is a cellular-scale Turing envelope (98.45 µm). Integer division 98450 nm / 2362 nm = 41, so forty-one takahashii detail wavelengths fit inside one suzukii envelope. Takahashii does not deploy that wing-spot prepattern; at 2.362 µm the pattern that remains is the subcellular pigment lattice, and k_c is ~41.7 times the suzukii envelope wavenumber.

successor.what_changes: The teissieri cellular envelope is 8550 nm longer than the suzukii envelope (107000 − 98450). That Holocene lengthening sits at the primordium tier and does not rescale the 2.362 µm takahashii lattice. Detail-scale k_c stays pinned by the Schnakenberg pair (a, b, Du, Dv) while the spot/ocellus envelope remains labile across the clade.

equations.kinetics: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + Du * laplacian(u); dv/dt = b - u^2 v + Dv * laplacian(v)
equations.critical_wavelength: lambda_c = 2 * pi / k_c, k_c = argmax sigma(k)
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic on a 28.344 µm square chart (12 critical wavelengths). Reconstructed local unfolding of the ocellar epithelium / fore-tibial transverse-row field, not a claim about the whole-animal boundary.

parameters.note: Chosen so the analytic dispersion peak sits on 2.362 µm. Not the alpha_scale/beta_offset pair used by the 98 µm takahashii, suzukii, or teissieri stub slots.

specimen_image.license_note: Gallery fallback. A Wikimedia Commons search on 2026-10-27 returned only File:Drosophila_pseudotakahashii.png (CC BY-SA 4.0), a different species; that file was not copied.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952: diffusion-driven instability and a finite critical wavelength
Schnakenberg 1979: two-species chemical kinetics with a cubic autocatalytic term
Murray 1981: coat-marking prepattern wavelength set by diffusion scale
Tanaka, Barmina & Kopp 2009 and Kopp 2011: sex-comb morphology diversifies by spatial doublesex/Scr regulation; transverse rows versus rotated combs
Atallah et al. 2014: D. suzukii ovipositor and the close relatives of the suzukii subgroup
reconstructed_in_script: Slot-specific (a, b, Du, Dv) placing lambda_c at 2.362 µm
Periodic 12-wavelength chart, explicit Euler, radial-FFT wavelength, dispersion Pearson/KS
Equal-diffusion ablation and the Dv sweep
Otsu segmentation of the gallery plate and the composite GIF
transfer_boundary: 2.362e-06 m is the campaign detail-scale assignment for this slot (log10=-5.627), not a wet-lab measurement quoted from a takahashii ocellus paper
Melanogaster rhabdomere diameters of order 1–2 µm motivate the tier but are not a takahashii measurement
The suzukii → takahashii → teissieri order is the project chronoseries index 37/41, not an anagenetic fossil sequence (all three are extant, 0 Ma)
does_not_claim: That a published measurement equals 2.362 µm on a D. takahashii ocellus
That D. takahashii carries the D. suzukii apical wing spot
That D. pseudotakahashii is an acceptable specimen proxy
That the gallery plate is a museum photograph with a documented CC deed beyond the project gallery fallback
